items.headline: Stocks end mixed Tuesday: Nasdaq +0.83%, S&P 500 +0.36%, Dow -0.38%
items.note: Chip stocks (AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Nvidia) lifted the Nasdaq and ended a three-day S&P losing streak, while Apple's weak margin forecast dragged the Dow down about 197 points. Election Day and a 10-year yield near 4.9% kept investors cautious.

items.headline: Treasury yields stay high as two Fed presidents say rates may need to rise
items.note: The 10-year yield edged up to about 4.91%. Higher yields make future company profits worth less today, which pressures tech and growth stocks, and affects the cost of loans for everyone.

items.headline: Apple falls 1.9% on weak holiday-quarter margin outlook
items.note: Apple warned that rising memory chip costs will squeeze margins, wiping out about $94 billion in market value. Memory costs are an AI-boom side effect that hits consumer hardware makers.

items.headline: AMD reports record $13.4B quarter; data center sales up 97%
items.note: AMD's data center revenue hit $8.5B, above its own forecast, showing AI chip demand still growing. Arista also beat, with revenue up 58.5%, while Palantir slipped despite 96% revenue growth because new US contract value grew only 11%.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO: still no price range or date as of Oct 30
items.note: The public S-1 was filed Oct 26 (ticker ANT, Nasdaq). The roadshow can't start before Nov 10; Bloomberg and the WSJ have reported different target weeks, and Reuters says investors are weighing a lower valuation. None of this is confirmed by the company.

items.headline: Chinese AI firms reportedly order $70B in Nvidia chips; Oracle drops Tencent chip deal
items.note: Bloomberg (via Techmeme) says Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance ordered about 6M chips, but only around 1% may arrive within four months. The FT reports Oracle scrapped a roughly $7B chip-leasing deal with Tencent after US government pressure. Both are secondhand summaries, not read at the original source.

items.headline: Election results raise questions about AI data center buildout
items.note: Bloomberg headlines summarized by LLM Stats say a Democratic sweep is prompting investors to rethink trades tied to AI infrastructure, and that gubernatorial wins could bring more scrutiny to data centers. StockTitan notes the same worry. Results are still being reported, so watch for details.

items.headline: Late-October model launches: GPT-6.1 Terra, Gemini 4 Carbon, Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.note: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra ($1/$5 per million tokens) targets high-volume computer-use tasks; Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is limited to cyber defenders with no public API; Moonshot promised open weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro by Nov 4. Specs are lab-reported.

learn.term: Discount rate (why higher yields hurt growth stocks)
learn.explain: A dollar next year is worth less than a dollar today, because you could earn interest on today's dollar. Investors 'discount' a company's future profits using an interest rate, usually tied to Treasury yields. When the 10-year yield rises, as it did to about 4.9% on Tuesday, those future profits are worth less in today's terms. The effect is biggest for growth companies, whose profits are expected far in the future, which is why tech stocks often wobble when yields climb.
